stem.en: Which type of muscle contracts according to our will, such as in the limbs?

whyWrong.en: Involuntary muscles work automatically in internal organs.
Cardiac muscle is specific to the heart.

explanation.en: Skeletal muscles of the limbs and neck are voluntary muscles.

stem.en: Regular physical activity helps increase HDL (good cholesterol) and decrease LDL (bad cholesterol).

explanation.en: Chapter 2 states exercise produces more HDL and less LDL.

stem.en: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart?

whyWrong.en: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
The aorta carries blood from the left ventricle to the body.

explanation.en: The pulmonary vein brings oxygen-rich blood from lungs to left atrium.

stem.en: Up to how many cc can vital capacity reach with regular exercise (according to Chapter 2)?

why.en: Chapter 2 mentions vital capacity can go up to 5500 cc.

explanation.en: Regular exercise can raise vital capacity up to 5500 cc.

stem.en: What is the temporary shortage created when oxygen demand during intense exercise exceeds intake?

why.en: Tidal volume is normal breath volume.

stem.en: Which large artery arises from the left ventricle to supply oxygenated blood to all organs?

whyWrong.en: Vena cava returns deoxygenated blood to the right atrium.
Bronchi are air passages in the lungs.

explanation.en: The aorta distributes oxygenated blood from the left ventricle.

stem.en: During inhalation, the diaphragm contracts and flattens, increasing thoracic cavity volume.

explanation.en: Contraction of the diaphragm and rib muscles expands the chest cavity so air rushes in.

stem.en: Low density lipoprotein (LDL) is commonly known as ___ cholesterol.

why.en: HDL is good cholesterol; LDL is bad cholesterol.

explanation.en: LDL adversely affects heart blood vessels and is called bad cholesterol.
